title: Aggrega Infrastructure Base (Recipe)
description: Ops-authored pointer and mapping layer connecting Dev intent to a specific infrastructure execution engine. Strictly 1:1 with a physical provider and catalog component.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the implementation recipe (e.g., 2.1.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

spec.description: The provider binding, source, value mapping, and pipeline for a Recipe. Supports three input kinds composed by addition: sourced (source plus valuesMapping overlay), synthesized (workload), and artifacts (named output files).

then.description: The eval provider executes formatting in-memory. Fetching a 'source', a 'workload', 'artifacts', or utilizing base mapping fields is mathematically banned.

else.description: Non-eval providers use the three-input-kinds model. At least one input kind must be present: sourced (source + values overlay), synthesized (workload), or artifacts. Pairing rules apply: valuesMapping pairs with source; and a workload: block requires a provider whose engine supports workload synthesis — a synthesized-mode Recipe bound to a non-synthesizing provider halts loudly at render time.

capability.description: The explicit render-engine capability this recipe binds to (e.g., 'helm', 'terraform', 'compose', 'eval') — the provider engine kind that renders it. Accepts an optional version pin, in the same three forms as 'implements': unversioned ('helm'), exact ('helm:1.0.0'), or major-compatible range ('helm:^1.0.0'). The bare name selects the engine kind; the pin, when present, selects which version of the provider-rendering plugin serving that engine renders this recipe — highest available when unpinned, exact for an exact pin, highest-in-range for a caret. A pin that no serving plugin version satisfies halts the build loudly. Everything downstream of engine selection — output grouping, path segments, pipeline compatibility, and codec choice — keys on the bare engine kind, so two recipes pinning different plugin versions of the same engine coexist in one build.

implements.description: Declares which catalog component type this recipe is able to implement (exact version 'core/api-server:1.0.0', major-compatible range 'core/api-server:^1.0.0', or unversioned 'core/api-server'). The compiler uses it to verify Manifest mappings and to suggest candidates in diagnostics and editor completion; it never resolves a build. The Manifest mapping is the user's explicit deployment choice, pinned in the lockfile.

source.description: The location of the infrastructure code. Accepts a Universal URI string, or an open structured object whose provider-defined keys are exposed to the Recipe's templates as '.source.*'.

oneOf.description: Universal URI string (e.g., './src', 'git::https://...', 'oci://...'). Used for local paths, OCI artifacts, and Git repositories.

Open Structured Object (additionalProperties: true). Its keys are provider-defined and are exposed to the Recipe's templates as '.source.*' (for example '.source.chart'). By design the core is schema-agnostic: each provider's WebAssembly socket is intended to define and validate its own source shape (such as 'registry'/'chart' for Helm, or 'workspace' for Terraform). CURRENT SHIPPED BEHAVIOR: per-provider Wasm source validation is not yet implemented. The core resolves a FETCHED source by the { kind, url, version } form, where 'kind' selects a built-in resolver (today: helm-oci-chart, helm-https-chart, compose-https-fragment). A fetch-intended source must therefore use { kind, url, version }; a structured source without 'kind'/'url' is not fetched, and if a fetch was intended it fails loudly at lock-time source descent rather than silently resolving to nothing. When the per-provider Wasm socket ships it will validate provider-specific shapes and translate them ahead-of-time into a deterministic { kind, url, version } fetch identity.

locals.description: The Private Ops State. Internal computation results available only within this Recipe's templates (valuesMapping, provides, pipeline[].with). Used to export physical realities (e.g., target containers, JSON paths) for downstream Wasm plugins. Never exposed to callers — use provides for the public API.

provides.description: The Public Developer API. Contractual output variables available for downstream Caller inject resolution. The compiler evaluates provides templates in Pass 1 (self-contained, any order). Callers resolve inject keys against these values in Pass 2. Values are scalars — the pipe carries them blindly and stringifies deterministically at the injection boundary.

valuesMapping.description: Values mapping content with three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar (typically block-scalar YAML `|`) producing the provider's expected values format from Aggrega context (.values, .secrets, .infra). Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.tmpl`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/mappings/<entry>`, referencing a MappingLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference).

workload.description: Workload YAML producer with three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output parses as 'aggrega.ai/v1alpha1 Workload'. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/workloads/<entry>`, referencing a WorkloadLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). The target Provider's engine must support workload synthesis; the standard-library catalog declares workloadSchema on such providers as the documented contract. A workload: Recipe bound to a provider whose engine cannot synthesize halts loudly at render time.

$import.description: A local file path, or a bare-name WorkloadLibrary reference `<Library>#/workloads/<entry>`. A registry host (`oci://…`) is rejected: a library is addressed by identity, and the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile.

artifacts.description: Map of output filename to artifact-content authoring. Each entry's value carries one of three modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output is the artifact body. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/artifacts/<entry>`, referencing an ArtifactsLibrary bundle by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). A bundle expands into one output per file, each named by the bundle's authored filename. Map keys become output filenames verbatim. Collisions across artifact entries, bundle files, source output, workload synthesis are load-time or render-time errors.

$import.description: A local file path, or a bare-name ArtifactsLibrary reference `<Library>#/artifacts/<entry>` (the entry names a bundle). A registry host (`oci://…`) is rejected: a library is addressed by identity, and the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile.

outputLabels.description: Recipe-author-declared labels stamped onto every object this recipe's rendered output produces, provider-translated onto each engine's label surface (Kubernetes metadata.labels for helm synthesis, source-render, and artifacts; Compose service labels; per-resource tags on Terraform .tf.json artifact bodies). They ride the same rail as the fixed provenance labels but are author-owned rather than compiler-owned. The aggrega.ai/ and app.kubernetes.io/ namespaces are reserved for platform-native provenance and are rejected at load. A key or value that is not a valid label for the target engine is the recipe author's responsibility; the core does not police label charset beyond the reserved-namespace rule.

pipeline.description: Sequential list of Wasm plugins to execute for stateful AST mutation directly on the base infrastructure.

id.description: A unique programmatic identifier for this step, allowing downstream plugins to reference its outputs.

plugin.description: The URI of the Plugin entity this step runs (e.g. `name:version` or `provider/name:version`). The entity's spec.plugin is the content-addressed .wasm artifact; the build resolves the entity to its artifact and loads the bytes. A bare .wasm or artifact reference is not accepted here.

function.description: The exported Wasm function to invoke.

with.description: Inline Go template evaluating to a JSON/YAML map that strictly satisfies this plugin's explicit input schema.

optional.description: When true, a failure of this step (a guest trap, a patch targeting a document not present in the set, a malformed patch, or an error-severity diagnostic) is downgraded to a loud warning: the pre-step document set is restored, this step's output is discarded, and the pipeline continues. When false or absent, any step failure halts the build after restoring the pre-step document set.

when.description: Inline Go template evaluated at pipeline-walk time. When it renders a falsy value the step is skipped — a pass-through: the document set flows to the next step unchanged, contributing no patches, side effects, or step record. An empty or absent `when` always runs the step. Truthiness follows the standard convention for boolean-like template output: the strings `true`/`True`/`TRUE`, any nonzero number, and any other non-empty string are true, while `false`/`False`/`FALSE`, the empty string, and zero are false. `when` and `optional` are independent: a step may declare both.

assertions.description: Build-time cross-field validation. Each entry is a named assertion: the key is a stable rule identifier surfaced in error messages; the value is a Go template string with `{{ fail "message" }}` halt semantics. Multiple named assertions per entity evaluate per-instance in author-declared order; the first failing assertion halts the build. Recipe assertions evaluate at Step 5b (post-binding, post-allProvides-evaluation, pre-render) and express implementation invariants of the specific wrapped chart or module. Template context: .values / .infra / .uses / .secrets / .metadata plus .provides / .locals / .recipe. The evaluator uses missingkey=error: references to undefined keys halt with a no-such-key diagnostic; optional-field idioms use Sprig default / hasKey.

sourceDigests.description: Content pins for the remote sources this recipe references, frozen at resolution from the fetched bytes and read back at build to verify the cached source has not drifted. Each entry mirrors the resolved-source identity {kind, url, chart, version} plus the content digest (and, for an OCI-distributed source, the manifest digest). One entry per distinct resolved-source identity the recipe fetches; a recipe whose source resolves to different identities per consuming instance carries one entry per identity. Local (filesystem-relative) sources are never pinned. Written by the resolution phase into a writable recipe file; a recipe fetched from a registry arrives pre-pinned.

kind.description: The resolved source kind (e.g. helm-oci-chart, helm-https-chart, compose-https-fragment, terraform-module-git).

url.description: The authored source URL the digest pins — the identity URL as written in spec.source.url (a repo root or a direct .tgz for helm-https). Build reconstructs this same URL offline, so it is the stable identity the pin is keyed on, not a resolved artifact location.

chart.description: The chart name for a repo-root helm source (spec.source.chart), part of the resolved-source identity so two charts served from one repo root at the same version pin distinctly. Absent for a direct .tgz, OCI, compose, or git source, where the URL alone identifies the artifact.

version.description: The concrete pinned version the source resolved to.

digest.description: The SHA-256 content digest (sha256:<hex>) of the fetched source archive, verified against the cached bytes at build.

manifestDigest.description: The OCI manifest digest for an OCI-distributed source — the independent root of trust. Present only for an OCI source (a helm-oci-chart); absent for an https or git source, which carries no manifest by construction.

artifactDigests.description: Content pins for the external files this recipe's artifacts import via $import, frozen at resolution and read back at build to verify the imported file has not drifted. One entry per artifact whose value is a file import; an inline (literal) artifact is already part of the entity and carries no separate pin. Written by the resolution phase into a writable recipe file.

name.description: The artifact key (the artifacts: map key) whose $import file this entry pins.

digest.description: The SHA-256 content digest (sha256:<hex>) of the imported file's bytes, verified at build.
